candidates.reason: Keeps the original left-to-right banner structure. Headline and subhead are grouped and share a left edge, and the CTA sits on the same axis. Flaws: the logo is small for the taller canvas, and the content band floats with a lot of empty space above and below.

The headline is pinned near the top and the subhead drops to the bottom, leaving a large dead gap that breaks the headline/subhead group. The logo and CTA sit at mid-height, so nothing shares a common horizontal axis.

The headline is centered while the subhead starts further left, under the logo, so they don't share an edge. The subhead crowds the bottom edge, the CTA is enlarged and jammed toward the right edge, and the logo is cramped between the text lines.

Hierarchy and reading order are wrecked. The logo is blown up to be the central focal point, the headline shrinks into a small left-edge label, the subhead is tiny, broken over two lines and stranded bottom-right away from the headline, and the CTA is undersized.
